summary:
The headline signal today is R1 and R2's starting-pitcher category running white-hot: 102-70 (59%) over the last 14 days versus a 52% season baseline, a +7.5pt spike on n=172 — that's the single strongest edge on the board right now. Pair that with the trends category riding a 3-game winning streak at 59% for R1/R2/R3, and any pick where those two categories agree is worth extra weight. On today's slate, that combo points hardest at COL @ ATL, where all four ratings stack on ATL with deltas between +2.25 and +2.62 — the largest consensus gap of the day — and Feltner's road ERA profile lines up with the SP category strength driving R1/R2. LAD @ DET is the mirror image: every rating fades LAD by at least -1.74, topping out at R4's -2.45, which is notable since R4 also owns the best short-term strong-play unit trail (7d +11.0u at 62%, 14d +16.0u at 63%). When R4 diverges that hard from the field on a fade, it's historically been the number to trust.

Steer clear of bullpen_fatigue-driven plays across the board — every rating is 44% over the last 14 days with a 4-game losing streak, so any pick leaning on bullpen fatigue as a tiebreaker (think BAL @ ATH or CHW @ MIN, both modest-consensus fades) should get downgraded a tick. Full 4-rating consensus also lines up on PHI @ LAA (fade PHI, -1.74 to -2.44) and TEX @ MIL, where MIL's split delta actually grows with each rating tier up to R4's +1.85 — worth noting since MIL is 65% (30-16) and 70% strong-play ROI (+13.0u) when the model likes them, one of the best team-when-liked profiles on the board. The two true split games, SFG/ARI and BOS/NYY, are where R1-R3 disagree with R4; with R4's hot short-term unit record, lean toward its side (ARI, NYY) rather than fading it blind. TBR remains a name to trust when picked (68%, +21.0u strong), and today's TBR lean, while modest in delta (+0.34 to +0.97), fits that profile.
